answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying each identity to a refundable stake plus a verifiable work history: new agents start with tiny, low-trust jobs and only earn bigger ones after peers attest their delivered work. A bridge between stake and reputation makes fake accounts expensive, because each copy must fund its own stake and build its own record. Like a reef, the network grows strong slowly from many small verified acts, and one onyx ledger entry of past work lets anyone check whether an agent is real or just another cheap clone.
